new_nodes.label: The 2026 federal general election is held on Tuesday 2026-11-03
new_nodes.basis: Statute: 2 U.S.C. 7 fixes the Tuesday after the first Monday in November as House election day, and that day in 2026 is November 3. A calendar rule, decided independent of any view on turnout or disputes.
new_nodes.rationale: The tree prices the post-election fight (midterms-2026) but has no clock row for the election itself. This row only claims voting is held on the statutory date in the states. SOFT part: a local postponement (storm, litigation) in one jurisdiction, and whether a stranger counts a Louisiana-style runoff or late-counted ballots as 'held'; the 0.99 is for the statutory date, not for the count.

gaps: The tree has no node for Supreme Court emergency-docket litigation, immigration enforcement (third-country removals, mandatory detention, birthright citizenship), the Voting Rights Act/redistricting landscape (Callais, new maps in 9-10 states), Fed independence (Cook, Slaughter) or ACA coverage removals; those events map to context at best. Tariff authority is the biggest unverified storyline: I confirmed the 2026-02-20 IEEPA ruling, the CIT and Federal Circuit steps on Section 122 and the 7/24 switch to Section 301, but not the current Federal Circuit status or any challenge to the new 301 tariffs, so tariff-legal-challenge (0.42) may be mispriced and I did not suggest a change. The 2026-10-22 housing executive order is unverified (the feed says signed; same-day Semafor/HousingWire say draft), and several feed items are re-runs of older events (birthright 6/30, Callais 4/29, pharma tariff 4/2, vaccine EO 8/10, Watson 6/29), so first-seen dates mislead; the feed also carries about 81 NCAA/Ohio items plus mosquito and AI-renaming orders that matter to nothing in the tree.
